core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Ghais corresponds to the Arabic form غيث (Arabic root غ ي ث (gh-y-th); غيث (Ghayth)). Its core sense is rain, succour, relief. Ghais is best identified with غيث (Ghayth) 'rain; succour, relief', the rain that rescues a parched land — an established Arabic male name. The source gave غيس in the script columns and glossed it 'helper, supporter', which fits the 'succour' sense of غيث. The source's 'helper, supporter' gloss and the spelling غيس are both non-standard for the word.
